---
title: "Examples"
subtitle: "Every colour format, marked."
description: "Each colour format recognised by the extension, shown in inline code and in prose, with its swatch drawn by the filter."
---

Every swatch below is drawn by the filter as this page is rendered.
The site scans both inline code and prose:

```yaml
extensions:
  preview-colour:
    code: true
    text: true
```

## Named colours

In code: `red`, `rebeccapurple`, `cornflowerblue`, `darkslategray`.

In prose: red, rebeccapurple, cornflowerblue, darkslategray.

Both British and American spellings are recognised, so `grey` and `gray` are marked alike.

## Hex

In code: `#441100`, `#b22222`, `#F03`.

In prose: #441100, #b22222, #F03.

Short hex works as well as the six-digit form.

## Functional forms

In code: `rgb(10, 100, 200)`, `rgb(10,100,200)`, `rgb(100%, 20%, 100%)`.

In prose: rgb(10, 100, 200), rgb(100%, 20%, 100%).

In code: `hsl(240, 100%, 50%)`, `hwb(135 0% 40%)`.

In prose: hsl(240, 100%, 50%), hwb(135 0% 40%).

Spaces after the commas are optional in every case.

## Transparency

In code: `rgba(255, 0, 0, 0.5)`, `rgba(255, 0, 0, 50%)`, `hsla(120, 100%, 50%, 0.25)`.

In prose: rgba(255, 0, 0, 0.5), hsla(120, 100%, 50%, 0.25).

This page is HTML, so the swatches above carry their alpha.
In a PDF, a Word file, or a deck the opaque colour is drawn instead, and the filter warns once.

## Keywords

In code: `currentColor`, `transparent`.

In prose: currentColor, transparent.

`currentColor` takes the colour of the surrounding text, and `transparent` is invisible by definition.
Neither has an equivalent outside HTML, so both are skipped there.

## What is not recognised

A colour in inline code has to be the whole of it.

| Written | Marked |
| --- | --- |
| `` `#441100` `` | Yes |
| `` `"My colour is #441100"` `` | No |
| `` `["#441100", "#114400"]` `` | No |

: Inline code is matched whole. {.striped .hover tbl-colwidths="[48,52]"}

Neither of the last two is marked above, which is the demonstration.

## Choosing the glyph

The swatch character is configurable, for every format at once or one at a time:

```yaml
extensions:
  preview-colour:
    glyph:
      default: "●"
      html: "&#9632;"
      latex: '\\textbullet'
      typst: "◆"
```

This site keeps the defaults, so the HTML swatches above are the fisheye `&#9673;`.

## Exporting the colours

Every colour found can be written out, for an audit or to extract a palette:

```yaml
extensions:
  preview-colour:
    json: my-colours.json
```

The file records the original text, the resolved hex, any alpha, and whether the colour came from code or prose.
This site leaves it off, since it would write a file into the project on every render.

## Source

The repository ships a short, standalone starting point you can copy: [`example.qmd`](https://github.com/mcanouil/quarto-preview-colour/blob/main/example.qmd).
